item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 290515
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Oct 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Vance, located about a couple hundred miles
west-northwest of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure could develop well to the southeast of
the Hawaiian Islands by this weekend or early next week. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear generally favorable for some slow
development of this system as it moves westward to
west-northwestward into the Central Pacific basin.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 290832
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026
 
...FLOOD AND MUDSLIDE THREAT CONTINUES FOR MEXICO DUE TO VANCE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.0N 108.4W
ABOUT 300 MI...480 KM WNW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 180 MI...290 KM WNW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 15 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1001 MB...29.56 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the west-central and northwestern coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 21.0 North, longitude 108.4 West. Vance is
moving toward the north-northeast near 7 mph (11 km/h). A turn to 
the north, followed by a decrease in forward speed, is expected 
over the next 24 hours.
 
Satellite data indicate that the maximum sustained winds are near 
40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts. Vance should gradually weaken 
today and is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low late 
today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1001 mb (29.56 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, far southwestern
Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, with isolated higher totals
of 7 inches possible over central and southern Sinaloa. This
rainfall may produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect coastal portions of
southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as the southern
portion of the Baja California Peninsula, during the next couple of
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 290835
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026

Vance has had an unusual structure overnight.  While obviously still 
a sheared tropical cyclone on satellite imagery, scatterometer data 
indicated that strong winds of about 40 kt were located well 
northeast (over 120 n mi) of the center under very deep convection, 
just downstream of the Islas Marias.  This atypical pattern of winds 
very distant from the center suggests that they were probably 
downdraft induced (or convective scale), possibly enhanced by 
terrain and not representative of the tropical cyclone, especially 
with rising pressures observed from the drifting buoy very near the 
center.  There were a couple of believable tropical-storm-force 
vectors closer to the center outside of the thunderstorm mass, so 
the initial intensity is set to 35 kt on this advisory.  

The storm hasn't moved much since the last advisory, with the 
center generally moving north-northeastward slowly.  Basically all 
of the model guidance suggest that the very strong shear will cause 
any deep convection to cease later today.  The evolution would 
cause the system to become very shallow, and it could get caught in 
any area of lighter low-level steering currents, keeping the system 
just offshore of Mexico before it likely degenerates into a trough 
of low pressure later on Friday. The new forecast is nudged to the 
left, toward the model consensus.  

While Vance has re-strengthened slightly, extremely strong vertical 
shear is expected to strip away any remaining associated convection 
later today and cause weakening before the winds could impact 
Mexico.  The new NHC forecast is similar to the previous one and is 
consistent with the latest ECMWF solution, which has had a good 
handle on the temporary re-intensification.  It should be emphasized 
that the main threat with Vance is the very heavy rainfall and high 
rain rates near the areas of very deep convection near the Islas 
Marias and southwestern Mexico.
 
 
Key Message:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact
portions of western Mexico during the next day or two. This rainfall
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern
Sinaloa, far southwestern Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  29/0900Z 21.0N 108.4W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  29/1800Z 22.0N 108.0W   30 KT  35 MPH
 24H  30/0600Z 23.4N 108.2W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  30/1800Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Blake
